coverage.audit_note: The revised manuscript has 34 numbered environments and 14 labelled equations. New exact-statement bridges and the quotient construction are tracked explicitly. Arithmetic-operation complexity and historical comparisons are expository; the checked exponent is defined through tensor rank. All mathematical entries have checked Lean declarations; the complete compilation, axiom audit, coverage checks, and tooling tests pass.

nodes.title: Finite tensors, restrictions, and equivalences
nodes.notes: This definition node records exactly the coordinate definitions in its statement, all of which are implemented. Its former open-ended proof plan bundled additional structural identities; individual proved operation laws are tracked in the dedicated restriction, power, permutation, and sum nodes. No unlisted associativity or distributivity theorem is claimed here.
nodes.statement_tex: A tensor over a field $F$ has three finite coordinate sets. A restriction is the image under three linear maps, and equivalence means mutual restriction. Define factor permutations, Kronecker products, powers, direct sums, and coordinate reindexings.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use finite coefficient arrays, finite-sum factor-map actions, and mutual restriction for equivalence. Define permutations by rearranging coordinate types, powers by finite tuples, direct sums by disjoint coordinate blocks, and reindexing by coordinate bijections. Operation laws are recorded in their separate support nodes.

nodes.title: Mutual restriction and invertible factor maps
nodes.notes: The final correspondence audit identified this prose assertion separately from the definition of equivalence. The checked proof works over every field, including zero tensors and empty coordinate spaces.
nodes.statement_tex: For tensors in the same ambient coordinate spaces, $T\cong S$ if and only if $S=(A\otimes B\otimes C)T$ for invertible matrices $A,B,C$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Mutual restriction preserves all flattening ranks. Each factor map is therefore injective on the corresponding tensor support. Extend its induced isomorphism of support subspaces to an ambient automorphism and replace the three factor maps successively. Inverse factor maps prove the converse.

nodes.title: Algebraic degeneration over every field
nodes.notes: The rational-function relation, its equivalence with polynomial witnesses, and all listed operation laws are checked over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: Write $T\trianglerighteq S$ when polynomial linear maps send $T$ to $\varepsilon^dS+\varepsilon^{d+1}E(\varepsilon)$ for some nonnegative integer $d$. This agrees with rational-function specialization in the paper. Degeneration is reflexive and transitive, contains restriction, and respects tensor products and direct sums.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Clear denominators and normalize the leading coefficient to compare the two definitions, as proved in the rational-degeneration support node. For composition substitute a sufficiently high power of the parameter before composing the polynomial witnesses. The parameter is formal, so no infinitude or characteristic assumption is introduced.

nodes.title: Diagonal tensors and rank invariants
nodes.notes: All seven definitions are checked. Subrank and border subrank are attained finite maxima; the positive-power subrank roots form a nonempty bounded set, so their real supremum agrees with the manuscript definition. Polynomial and rational degeneration are equivalent over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: Define $\langle r\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^r e_i\otimes e_i\otimes e_i$. Rank and border rank are the least $r$ such that $\langle r\rangle$ restricts or degenerates to $T$. Subrank and border subrank reverse these relations. Define $\widetilde R(T)=\inf_{n\ge1}R(T^{\otimes n})^{1/n}$ and $\widetilde Q(T)=\sup_{n\ge1}Q(T^{\otimes n})^{1/n}$.

nodes.title: Asymptotic rank calculus
nodes.notes: All stated laws and the comparison with the manuscript rational-function degeneration relation are checked over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: Rank is monotone under restriction and submultiplicative. Its normalized powers converge to asymptotic rank. Asymptotic rank is power multiplicative, submultiplicative, subadditive, and monotone under degeneration; in particular $\widetilde R(T)\le\underline R(T)\le R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use submultiplicativity and the subadditive-sequence limit theorem. To handle a polynomial degeneration witness, extract coefficient $dN$ after taking $N$ powers. There are only polynomially many triples of coefficient maps, giving a polynomial overhead times $R(T^{\otimes N})$. Its $N$-th root tends to one over every field. Derive subadditivity by the binomial expansion and uniform exponential rank bounds.

nodes.title: Flattenings and their ranks
nodes.notes: All stated laws are checked. The rational/polynomial degeneration equivalence transfers monotonicity to the manuscript relation.
nodes.statement_tex: Each tensor determines three flattening matrices. Their ranks are monotone under restriction and degeneration, multiplicative under Kronecker product, and bounded above by tensor rank.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use the checked flattening product and power identities. Group each flattening into a matrix tensor and transport the polynomial degeneration witness by Kronecker products of the complementary factor maps. Its asymptotic rank equals matrix rank, so asymptotic-rank monotonicity gives degeneration monotonicity.

nodes.title: Flattening lower bounds
nodes.notes: The library also retains the stronger border-rank lower bound as auxiliary coverage.
nodes.statement_tex: For every tensor $T$ and each factor $i$, $R^{(i)}(T)\le\widetilde R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Tensor-power multiplicativity and the ordinary-rank bound give $R^{(i)}(T)^N\le R(T^{\otimes N})$. Take positive-power roots and then their infimum.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local proof using tensor-power multiplicativity and the infimum of rank roots.

nodes.title: Matrix multiplication and its exponent
nodes.notes: The coordinate formula, exponent definition, and all three special-shape equivalences are checked. The coordinate equivalences also hold at size zero and over any commutative semiring.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive integers $\ell,m,n$, define $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k}e_{ij}\otimes e_{jk}\otimes e_{ik}$. For every field $F$, set $\omega_F=\log_2\widetilde R_F(\langle2,2,2\rangle)$. The special shapes have the coordinate presentations $\langle n,1,1\rangle\cong\sum_i e_i\otimes e_1\otimes e_i$, $\langle1,n,1\rangle\cong\sum_i e_i\otimes e_i\otimes e_1$, and $\langle1,1,n\rangle\cong\sum_i e_1\otimes e_i\otimes e_i$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use the checked coordinate formula and exponent definition. Construct the three special-shape equivalences by removing singleton coordinates in the factor index types and applying coordinate reindexing.

nodes.title: Matrix multiplication as a bilinear structure tensor
nodes.notes: The final audit identified this interpretation as a separate background assertion. The contraction identity holds over semirings, and the literal structure-tensor equality is checked over every field. Zero dimensions are included.
nodes.statement_tex: Contracting the first two factors of $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle$ with matrices $X,Y$ gives the entries of $XY$. In the standard matrix bases, this coefficient tensor equals the structure tensor of the bilinear multiplication map.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Expand matrix multiplication as a finite sum and evaluate the equality indicators in the coefficient tensor. Compute the product of standard basis matrices to identify all structure-tensor coefficients.

nodes.title: Basic bounds for the exponent
nodes.notes: Both bounds are checked over every field. The lower bound comes from the first flattening; the upper bound comes from the elementary eight-term decomposition at matrix size two.
nodes.statement_tex: For every field $F$, $2\le\omega_F\le3$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The square matrix multiplication tensor has flattening rank $n^2$ and the elementary decomposition has $n^3$ terms. Apply these bounds at $n=2$ and use monotonicity of logarithms.

nodes.title: Matrix size independence of the exponent
nodes.notes: Checked in the power formulation over every field for every natural n with 1 <= n, including scalar multiplication. The manuscript leaves positivity implicit in Definition 2.4; Lean retains the explicit hypothesis. This proof needs neither numerical bounds on omega nor the rational/polynomial degeneration comparison.
nodes.statement_tex: For every field $F$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\widetilde R_F(\langle n,n,n\rangle)=n^{\omega_F}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply the monotone-power-function theorem to $f(n)=\widetilde R(\langle n,n,n\rangle)$. Dimension restrictions give monotonicity, scalar multiplication gives $f(1)=1$, and the tensor-power coordinate equivalence together with asymptotic-rank power multiplicativity gives $f(n^k)=f(n)^k$.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The explicit floor/ceiling tensor-power sandwich and rank-root limit prove size independence; scalar multiplication covers n=1.

nodes.title: Polynomial multiplication tensors
nodes.notes: The coefficient-vector expansion is checked against ordinary polynomial multiplication over any commutative semiring.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive integers $a,b$, define $\mathrm{PM}_{a,b}=\sum_{i=0}^{a-1}\sum_{j=0}^{b-1}e_i\otimes e_j\otimes e_{i+j}$. This is the structure tensor of multiplication of polynomials of degree less than $a$ and $b$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Expand the two finite sums of monomials, multiply them, and extract the coefficient at each output index.

nodes.title: Rank descent through a finite extension
nodes.notes: The finite-degree rank descent is checked for arbitrary field extensions and finite tensor coordinate types, including zero tensors. The proof uses an arbitrary basis of the extension and a linear retraction of the algebra map.
nodes.statement_tex: If $E/F$ has finite degree $k$ and $T$ is defined over $F$, then $R_F(T)\le k^2R_E(T_E)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Choose any basis of the extension over the base field and a linear left inverse of the algebra map. Expand the first two factors of every extension-field pure summand in this basis and retract the remaining coefficient to the base field. Each summand gives at most $k^2$ pure summands. A basis containing one is unnecessary.

nodes.title: Ranks of polynomial multiplication
nodes.notes: The small-field hypothesis makes the ceiling logarithm greater than one, so the maximum in the stronger uniform library bound can be removed. Interpolation includes the scalar case; the exact border and asymptotic ranks hold over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive $a,b$, a field with at least $a+b-2$ elements satisfies $R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})=a+b-1$. Over a finite field of size $q<a+b-2$, $R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})\le(a+b-1)\lceil\log_q(a+b-2)\rceil^2$. Over every field, $\underline R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})=\widetilde R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})=a+b-1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use finite evaluations and a leading-coefficient summand whose output polynomial is $X^{a+b-2}$ minus its finite-node interpolant. This gives $a+b-1$ pure summands at the sharp field-size threshold; the third flattening gives the matching lower bound. For finite fields choose the checked degree-$k$ extension with cardinality $q^k$, where $k=\lceil\log_q(a+b-2)\rceil>1$, and apply scalar descent. The existing uniform diagonal degeneration and flattening bound give the exact border and asymptotic ranks.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local interpolation and extension proof; imports the field-descent and specialization inequalities as ingredients.

nodes.title: Equal-block asymptotic sum identity
nodes.notes: Checked for every field K and all positive natural a,b, including a=1 and b=1. Repeated copies use explicit block-labelled coordinates. The revised manuscript explicitly supplies the integer rounding argument. The existing cor: label is preserved although the active environment is a lemma.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive integers $a,b$, $\widetilde R(\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a})=ab^\omega$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The repeated-copy upper bound and the square-size identity give $\widetilde R(\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a})\le ab^\omega$. For the lower bound, treat $a=1$ by selecting the sole block. For $a\ge2$, set $r_n=R(\langle2,2,2\rangle^{\otimes n})$, $q=\widetilde R(\langle2,2,2\rangle)>1$, and $p=\widetilde R(\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a})/b^\omega\ge1$. The matrix capacity comparison gives $q^n\le p^m$ whenever $r_n\le a^m$. Apply the integer-capacity growth lemma and the root-limit characterization to get $a\le p$.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Explicit short proof after acknowledging the asymptotic sum inequality of Schonhage; a reproof of prior work.

nodes.title: Finite probability distributions and entropy
nodes.notes: The definition extends to finite real weight vectors; probability nonnegativity and unit-sum conditions are hypotheses of the inequalities. Lean uses Real.log 0 = 0, giving the required zero-weight convention.
nodes.statement_tex: For a probability distribution $q$ on a nonempty finite set, define $H(q)=-\sum_iq_i\log_2q_i$, with $0\log0=0$.

nodes.title: Multinomial entropy limit and approximation with fixed support
nodes.notes: The original entropy proof now has checked multinomial asymptotics and rational approximation with exactly unchanged support. Zero counts are included in the limit. Rounded-up natural counts give positive denominators at every approximation stage. The entropy-weighted product passes to the limit even when fixed block values vanish. These results are independent of the alternative multinomial-sum proof used on the main theorem path.
nodes.statement_tex: If nonnegative integers $K_i$ sum to $K>0$ and $q_i=K_i/K$, then $\binom{nK}{nK_1,\ldots,nK_m}^{1/(nK)}\longrightarrow2^{H(q)}$. Every probability distribution is a limit of rational probability distributions with exactly the same support. Entropy-weighted product inequalities for rational probabilities therefore extend to all probabilities, including zero block values.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Stirling's formula gives $\log((nc)!)/n-c\log n\to c\log c-c$, treating $c=0$ separately. Sum over the counts and cancel the $K\log n$ terms, then divide by $K$ and exponentiate. For approximation, take $c_r(i)=\lceil(r+1)q_i\rceil$ and normalize by $\sum_i c_r(i)$. Zero coordinates stay zero and the normalized counts converge to $q$. Continuity of $x\log x$ gives entropy convergence; unchanged zero coordinates handle the otherwise discontinuous $0^0$ corner in the weighted products.

nodes.title: Entropy variational identity
nodes.notes: The full maximum is proved as an IsGreatest statement, including attainment. Normalized coordinates give a maximizer for positive total mass; a point mass handles zero total mass. Zero coordinates respect the convention 0^0=1. This result remains independent of the main theorem's direct multinomial proof.
nodes.statement_tex: For a nonempty finite set $I$ and $a_i\ge0$, $\max_q 2^{H(q)}\prod_i a_i^{q_i}=\sum_i a_i$, where $q$ ranges over probability distributions and $0^0=1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The checked weighted AM--GM inequality gives the upper bound. If the total mass is positive, set $q_i=a_i/\sum_j a_j$ and use the entropy product identity to obtain equality, treating zero coordinates explicitly. If the total mass is zero, choose a point mass; the upper bound and nonnegativity give equality. Record attainment and the upper bound together as a maximum.

nodes.title: Partially direct sums
nodes.notes: Implemented for every finite family with a common first coordinate space and dependent second/third coordinate spaces; the empty family is included.
nodes.statement_tex: For $T_h\in U\otimes V_h\otimes W_h$, define $\mathop{\diamondplus}_hT_h$ using the canonical inclusions into $U\otimes(\bigoplus_hV_h)\otimes(\bigoplus_hW_h)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use tagged basis indices in the second and third factors. The coefficient is the corresponding block coefficient when the tags match and zero otherwise.

nodes.title: Partial-sum calculus
nodes.notes: All six items are checked over commutative semirings, including zero repeated copies. The common first-factor map is fixed in the partial-sum reindexings.
nodes.statement_tex: A partially direct sum restricts to each summand. Partial sums are commutative and associative up to the canonical equivalences, and Kronecker products distribute over them on either side. Moreover, $T^{\diamondplus r}\cong T\otimes\langle1,1,r\rangle$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Construct the coordinate inclusions, projections, and reindexings. Every identity must keep the common first-factor map consistent.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The manuscript supplies a proof environment saying Straightforward.

nodes.title: The common-factor compatibility caveat
nodes.notes: Both negative assertions are checked over every field. The same first-factor map is sufficient to assemble restrictions; common maps in both directions suffice for equivalences. The explicit counterexample uses scalar blocks supported at one shared basis vector versus two distinct basis vectors.
nodes.statement_tex: Separate equivalences $S_h\cong T_h$ do not in general induce an equivalence of their partially direct sums: they can use incompatible maps on the common factor. The analogous implication for restrictions also fails.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use a common first-factor matrix and block-diagonal matrices on the other factors to assemble compatible maps. For the counterexample, each block is a scalar tensor supported at $e_0$ or $e_1$. The partial sum with both blocks at $e_0$ has first-flattening rank $1$, while the sum with blocks at $e_0,e_1$ has rank $2$. Flattening monotonicity excludes a restriction, and hence an equivalence, although the individual blocks are equivalent.

nodes.title: Separation by polynomial multiplication
nodes.notes: The full separation statement is checked over every field. The implementation also handles empty families and zero auxiliary size; the intermediate weighted degeneration holds over commutative semirings.
nodes.statement_tex: Let $T=\mathop{\diamondplus}_{h=1}^mT_h$ with $m,r\ge1$. Then $T^{\oplus(m+r-1)}\trianglerighteq(\bigoplus_{h=1}^mT_h)\otimes\langle1,1,r\rangle$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Degenerate the diagonal auxiliary tensor to polynomial multiplication. With zero-based indices use weights $i^2$, $h^2+2hj$, and $D-2hk$, choosing $D$ large enough to keep every weight nonnegative. Supported terms have total weight $D+(i-h)^2$, so the leading terms separate the blocks. Coordinate pullbacks identify the target with an ordinary direct sum tensored with $\langle1,1,r\rangle$.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Explicit parameter-weight construction in the proof following the statement.

nodes.title: Separation of a multinomial type class
nodes.notes: Checked with the exact multinomial coefficient and exact factor 2Q-1. Zero counts, N=0, and empty families are included. Independent first-factor equivalences are used only after ordinary separation.
nodes.statement_tex: For nonnegative counts $N_h$ with sum $N$ and $Q=\binom{N}{N_1,\ldots,N_m}$, $(T^{\otimes N})^{\oplus(2Q-1)}\trianglerighteq(\bigotimes_hT_h^{\otimes N_h})^{\oplus Q}\otimes\langle1,1,Q\rangle$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Expand the tensor power as a partial sum indexed by words, restrict to the specified type class, and apply separation with $m=r=Q$. Only after obtaining an ordinary direct sum identify the equivalent blocks by permuting tensor-power positions. Include the zero-count and $N=0$ unit conventions.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local type-class restriction and separation argument.

nodes.title: Kronecker symmetrization
nodes.notes: Checked as the product of the three even and three odd factor permutations, each occurring exactly once. The explicit six orders are identified bijectively with S3.
nodes.statement_tex: Define $T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3}=\bigotimes_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_3}\pi\cdot T$, using all six permutations of the three tensor factors.

nodes.title: Symmetrization identities
nodes.notes: All four properties are checked over commutative semirings, including zero dimensions and zero copies. Permutation invariance quantifies over the actual symmetric group; diagonal and matrix identities use explicit coordinate equivalences.
nodes.statement_tex: Symmetrization is invariant under permuting tensor factors and commutes with Kronecker product up to equivalence. It takes $T^{\oplus r}$ to $(T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3})^{\oplus r^6}$ and takes $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle$ to $\langle(\ell mn)^2,(\ell mn)^2,(\ell mn)^2\rangle$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Construct finite index equivalences for the six factors. Combine the coordinate formulas for direct sums and matrix multiplication.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The manuscript supplies a proof environment saying Straightforward.

nodes.title: Fractional symmetrized value
nodes.notes: The value is defined directly as the witness supremum in the extended nonnegative reals, and agrees exactly with rational-function witnesses. The zero tensor has no witnesses, so its value follows from the empty supremum without a separate branch. Lean extends the formula to all real parameters; the paper uses positive parameters. The revised definition explicitly uses the extended supremum and derives the zero value from it.
nodes.statement_tex: For $\tau>0$, let $V_\tau(T)$ be the supremum in $[0,+\infty]$ of $\bigl(ab^{3\tau}/(cd^{3\tau})\bigr)^{1/(6N)}$ over positive integers $a,b,c,d,N$ satisfying $\langle d,d,d\rangle^{\oplus c}\otimes(T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3})^{\otimes N}\trianglerighteq\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a}$. For $T=0$ the witness set is empty, so $V_\tau(0)=0$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Transfer polynomial and rational-function witnesses in both directions without changing their parameters or scores, then identify the two indexed suprema.

nodes.title: The exponent convention
nodes.notes: Expository convention; no separate Lean theorem is required.
nodes.statement_tex: The power $3\tau$ in the definition agrees with the convention that matrix multiplication has value $(\ell mn)^\tau$.

nodes.title: Sharp matrix-multiplication border-subrank lower bound
nodes.notes: The sharp cited lower bound is checked over every field, including dimension zero. The explicit monomial degeneration works over every commutative semiring. The central-band cardinality and its equality to the ceiling formula are proved exactly. Lemma 4.5 continues to use the simpler quadratic construction. The sharp construction is additional checked support for the manuscript’s cited bound.
nodes.statement_tex: For every positive integer $n$, $\underline Q(\langle n,n,n\rangle)\ge\lceil3n^2/4\rceil$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Set $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and retain triples $(i,j,i+j-m)$ for $0\le i,j<n$ and $m\le i+j<m+n$. The two removed triangular corners have total size $\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lceil n/2\rceil$, leaving $\lceil3n^2/4\rceil$ labels. Use weights $(i+j)^2$, $n^2+u^2-j^2$, and $4n^2-2i(i+z)$. On the tensor support $u+j=i+z$, their total is $5n^2+(i-u)^2$, whose minimum occurs exactly at diagonal labels. Reindex those labels by their cardinality and apply the border-subrank definition.

nodes.title: Value outside the admissible interval
nodes.notes: The full manuscript lemma is checked, with its positive-parameter hypothesis explicit. A stronger exact finiteness criterion holds for the library definition at every real parameter. The proof uses finite-unit normalization and a direct q² diagonal degeneration from matrix multiplication of size2q; it uses no sharper bound; the cited ceil(3n²/4) estimate is now also checked separately.
nodes.statement_tex: For $T\ne0$ and $\tau>0$ outside $[2/3,\omega/3]$, $V_\tau(T)=+\infty$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: If a nonzero tensor has finite value, monotonicity makes the unit value finite. The finite-unit lemma then forces $3\tau\le\omega$. The explicit degeneration $\langle2q,2q,2q\rangle\trianglerighteq\langle q^2\rangle$ and normalization give $q^2\le(2q)^{3\tau}$ for every positive integer $q$, hence $2\le3\tau$. Therefore all parameters outside the interval have infinite value. Combine this with the independently checked finiteness within the interval for an exact criterion.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local derivation, using the cited matrix-multiplication border-subrank bound as an input.

nodes.title: Witness bounds and finiteness without circularity
nodes.notes: Checked over every field, including T=0 and omega=2. No value identity or prior finiteness assumption is used. Equality with the manuscript rational-function value is now proved separately.
nodes.statement_tex: For $2/3\le\tau\le\omega/3$, every defining witness score is bounded by $\widetilde R(T)$. Consequently $V_\tau(T)\le\widetilde R(T)<+\infty$. For nonzero $T$ the witness set is nonempty and $V_\tau(T)\ge1$; the unit diagonal has value exactly one in the admissible interval.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: At the upper endpoint apply the equal-block asymptotic sum identity, degeneration monotonicity, and $\widetilde R(T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3})\le\widetilde R(T)^6$ to obtain $ab^\omega\le cd^\omega\widetilde R(T)^{6N}$. At the lower endpoint use flattening-rank monotonicity, the repeated-block formula, and $R_1(T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3})\le\widetilde R(T)^6$ to obtain the quadratic analogue. Bound intermediate witness scores by endpoint monotonicity of $(b/d)^{3\tau}$, then take the extended-real supremum. The all-one witness gives the lower bound; diagonal normalization gives unit value.

nodes.title: Fractional value calculus
nodes.notes: All six properties are checked. Permutation invariance follows directly from the defining witness set and equivalence of the symmetrizations, as in the updated manuscript. Positive-power, product, and scaling laws hold for all real parameters; the zero-power case uses unit normalization in the admissible interval. Matrix dimensions are positive as in Definition 2.4.
nodes.statement_tex: For every $\tau>0$, value in $[0,+\infty]$ is monotone under degeneration and invariant under factor permutation. For $n\ge1$, $V_\tau(T^{\otimes n})=V_\tau(T)^n$. Moreover $V_\tau(T\otimes S)\ge V_\tau(T)V_\tau(S)$, $V_\tau(\langle r\rangle\otimes T)=rV_\tau(T)$, and $V_\tau(\langle\ell,m,n\rangle\otimes T)=(\ell mn)^\tau V_\tau(T)$ for positive matrix dimensions, with $0\cdot\infty=0$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Transport witnesses under degeneration of the symmetrizations. Cross-power two witnesses to prove product supermultiplicativity, and transfer witnesses both into and out of tensor powers to prove equality. Absorb a diagonal or matrix block into denominator sizes for one inequality and numerator sizes for the reverse. Use extended-real supremum identities directly; restrict the power law to positive powers.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local proof of the listed value properties.

nodes.title: Normalization at the unit tensor
nodes.notes: Checked in aux:value-finiteness, with exact equality of the polynomial and rational-function definitions supplied by def:fractional-value.
nodes.statement_tex: For $2/3\le\tau\le\omega/3$, $V_\tau(\langle1\rangle)=1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The identity degeneration gives the lower bound. Apply the witness bound to the unit, whose asymptotic rank is one. Endpoint monotonicity bounds each witness score directly.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local witness-ratio bounds split into b <= d and b > d, using flattening rank and asymptotic rank.

nodes.title: Diagonal and matrix multiplication normalization
nodes.notes: Checked over every field in the admissible parameter interval. Matrix dimensions are positive; diagonal normalization also includes size zero.
nodes.statement_tex: In the admissible interval, $V_\tau(\langle r\rangle)=r$ and $V_\tau(\langle\ell,m,n\rangle)=(\ell mn)^\tau$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply the two exact scaling laws with the unit tensor.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local deduction from the value properties and unit normalization.

nodes.title: Value between asymptotic subrank and rank
nodes.notes: Both inequalities are checked over every field, including the zero tensor. The value is proved finite before passing to real numbers. The lower bound takes the supremum of the individual positive-power root bounds directly, without invoking convergence.
nodes.statement_tex: For $2/3\le\tau\le\omega/3$, $\widetilde Q(T)\le V_\tau(T)\le\widetilde R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use a maximal diagonal restriction, monotonicity, and diagonal normalization to get $Q(T^{\otimes N})\le V_\tau(T)^N$ for each $N\ge1$. Take roots and then the supremum from the definition of asymptotic subrank. Combine this with the independently checked upper bound from witness finiteness. No subrank limit theorem is needed.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local proof takes positive-power roots, then the supremum of subrank roots and infimum of rank roots.

nodes.title: Entropy bound for partially direct sums
nodes.notes: Checked for every real probability vector, including zero probabilities and zero block values. The proof uses the already checked superadditivity inequality and weighted AM-GM; no entropy limit or rational approximation is assumed.
nodes.statement_tex: For an admissible $\tau$, $T=\mathop{\diamondplus}_{h=1}^mT_h$, and a probability distribution $q$ on the blocks, $V_\tau(T)\ge2^{\tau H(q)}\prod_hV_\tau(T_h)^{q_h}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply the weighted AM--GM entropy bound to the finite block values, obtaining an upper bound by $(\sum_h V_\tau(T_h)^{1/\tau})^\tau$. Superadditivity and positivity of $\tau$ bound this by $V_\tau(T)$.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local multinomial type extraction and limiting argument.

nodes.title: Comparison with the laser-method estimate
nodes.notes: The Strassen tensor construction, exact border and asymptotic ranks, value inequality, and strict decimal upper bound are checked over every field. The proof uses binary partial-sum superadditivity, which gives the same bound as the equal-weight entropy inequality here. It does not use the main nine-quarters theorem. The historical attribution and comparison with other methods remain expository.
nodes.statement_tex: The entropy coefficient $\tau\ge2/3$ improves the coefficient $2/3$ from the cited laser-method estimate. For $n\ge1$, Strassen's tensor $S_n=\langle n,1,1\rangle\diamondplus\langle1,n,1\rangle$ has border rank and asymptotic rank $n+1$. For every admissible $\tau$, $(2n)^\tau\le V_\tau(S_n)\le n+1$. Taking $\tau=\omega/3$ and $n=3$ yields $\omega\le3\log4/\log6<2.32112$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The coefficient of $\varepsilon$ in $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(y_0+\varepsilon y_i)(z_0+\varepsilon z_i)-(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i)y_0z_0$ is $S_n$. This gives a degeneration from $\langle n+1\rangle$ over every field. An identity submatrix of the second flattening gives the matching lower bound. Each scalar-multiplication block has value $n^\tau$; binary superadditivity gives $(2n)^\tau$. Specialize to $n=3$, take logarithms, and certify the decimal comparison by exact rational bounds for $\log4$ and $\log6$.

nodes.title: Superadditivity for partially direct sums
nodes.notes: Checked over every field, including empty families and zero-valued blocks. The Lean proof reverses the manuscript order: superadditivity is proved first by summing finite type bounds, and the entropy bound follows afterward. The alternative proof is documented here rather than in a manuscript annotation.
nodes.statement_tex: For $2/3\le\tau\le\omega/3$ and $T=\mathop{\diamondplus}_hT_h$, $V_\tau(T)^{1/\tau}\ge\sum_hV_\tau(T_h)^{1/\tau}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Write $a_h=V_\tau(T_h)^{1/\tau}$ and $B=V_\tau(T)^{1/\tau}$. Type separation and exact value scaling give $Q^\tau\prod_hV_\tau(T_h)^{c_h}\le2V_\tau(T)^N$. Raise to $1/\tau$ and apply the checked multinomial-sum bound with $C=2^{1/\tau}$. Admissible finiteness justifies real arithmetic; transfer the result back to extended nonnegative reals.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local optimization of the preceding inequality.

nodes.title: Degeneration from compatible bilinear maps
nodes.notes: The revised weaker hypotheses exactly match the compatible-map theorem. Arbitrary finite bases are allowed, with the shared first-factor basis preserved. The short-exact-sequence theorem is retained as a special case.
nodes.statement_tex: Let $\iota_V:V_0\to V$, $\pi_V:V\to V_1$, $\iota_W:W_0\to W$, and $\pi_W:W\to W_1$ be linear maps. Assume $\pi_V$ is surjective, $\iota_W$ is injective, and $\pi_W\iota_W=0$. If bilinear maps satisfy $\varphi(u,\iota_Vv_0)=\iota_W\varphi_0(u,v_0)$ and $\varphi_1(u,\pi_Vv)=\pi_W\varphi(u,v)$, their structure tensors satisfy $T\trianglerighteq T_0\diamondplus T_1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Choose a linear left inverse of the output inclusion and a linear right inverse of the input quotient. Compatibility gives the two prescribed diagonal blocks; the zero composite on the output side makes the remaining required block zero. The structure-tensor action lemma translates input precomposition and output postcomposition into coefficient maps, and the checked split-map criterion gives the degeneration.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Explicit splitting and parameter maps in the local proof.

nodes.title: Polynomial multiplication concavity degeneration
nodes.notes: The checked coefficient theorem is stronger: a and p may be zero and b need only be at least one. The repeated model is canonically equivalent to the displayed matrix-product tensor, with a literal common first factor. The general exact-sequence lemma remains separate.
nodes.statement_tex: For $a,p\ge1$ and $b\ge2$, $\mathrm{PM}_{a,b}\otimes\langle1,1,p+1\rangle\trianglerighteq(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b-1}\otimes\langle1,1,p\rangle)\diamondplus\mathrm{PM}_{a,b+p}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use multiplication by $x-y$ and the boundary monomial section as input maps. Use diagonal-tail extraction and evaluation at $y=x$ as output maps. Check the three split-map identities coefficientwise and apply the order-one degeneration criterion. The revised abstract lemma uses weaker compatibility hypotheses; the concrete coefficient proof remains a direct implementation of the same block identities.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local exact-sequence proof, following acknowledged prior ideas.

nodes.title: Concavity of polynomial multiplication value
nodes.notes: Checked for all natural a,p and b at least one; zero multiplicity is handled as equality. No degeneration is left as an assumption.
nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$, let $P(a,b)=V_\tau(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})^{1/\tau}$. If $a,p\ge1$ and $b\ge2$, $(p+1)P(a,b)\ge pP(a,b-1)+P(a,b+p)$. In particular, $P(a,\cdot)$ is discretely concave.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply monotonicity and partial-sum superadditivity to the preceding degeneration, then use matrix multiplication scaling to pull out $p$ and $p+1$.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local deduction from the concavity degeneration.

nodes.title: Three-block polynomial multiplication degeneration
nodes.notes: The coefficient degeneration is proved over every commutative semiring. It retains the identical first-factor map in all three blocks.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive $a,b,c,d$, $\mathrm{PM}_{a,a+b+c+d-1}\trianglerighteq\mathrm{PM}_{a,b}\diamondplus(23)\cdot\mathrm{PM}_{a,c}\diamondplus\mathrm{PM}_{a,d}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Partition the second and third index sets into the three intervals in the manuscript. Two off-diagonal blocks receive a positive parameter weight and vanish. Reindex the surviving middle block in reverse order to identify the transposed polynomial multiplication tensor. All reindexings act identically on the shared first factor.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Explicit local block construction, following acknowledged prior ideas.

nodes.title: Tripling inequality
nodes.notes: The general three-block value inequality is checked before specializing all four sizes to a.
nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$ and positive $a$, $P(a,4a-1)\ge3P(a,a)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Set $a=b=c=d$ in the preceding degeneration, use permutation invariance of the value, and apply partial-sum superadditivity.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local deduction from the three-block degeneration.

nodes.title: Polynomial value satisfies the numerical hypotheses
nodes.notes: All numerical hypotheses are now supplied by the defined polynomial value over every field. The only parameter assumptions are admissibility; no tensor inequalities are assumed.
nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$, the function $P(a,b)=V_\tau(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})^{1/\tau}$ is symmetric, satisfies $P(1,a)=a$, and satisfies the concavity and tripling inequalities. These properties are packaged as the numerical growth hypotheses.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Identify $\mathrm{PM}_{1,a}$ with $\langle1,1,a\rangle$ and interchange the first two factors for symmetry. Combine normalization with the two polynomial-value inequalities.

nodes.title: Diagonal recurrence
nodes.notes: The generic numerical recurrence is now instantiated with the checked polynomial-value hypotheses.
nodes.statement_tex: For the manuscript function $P(a,b)=V_\tau(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})^{1/\tau}$ with admissible $\tau$, $P(a+1,a+1)\ge\frac{(3a+1)(3a+2)}{3a(3a-1)}P(a,a)$ for $a\ge1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply concavity first with $(b,p)=(a+1,3a-2)$ and then with $(b,p)=(a+1,3a+2)$. Use symmetry and tripling, collect the repeated $P(a+1,a+1)$ term, and divide only by strictly positive denominators.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Derived inside the proof of lem:4/3.

nodes.title: Quantitative Gamma-function growth
nodes.notes: Both inequalities hold uniformly for every positive integer. The Gamma sharpening is independent of the elementary main-theorem route. The asymptotic coefficient is recorded separately under Remark 6.2.
nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$ and $a\ge1$, $P_\tau(a,a)\ge G(a)\ge a^{4/3}$, where $G(a)=\frac{3a-1}{2\Gamma(4/3)}\frac{\Gamma(a+1/3)}{\Gamma(a)}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The Gamma expression equals one at $a=1$ and its successive ratio is the recurrence multiplier. Induction proves the first inequality. The same multiplier dominates $((a+1)/a)^{4/3}$, proving the second inequality by induction.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local recurrence, finite-product/Gamma identity, and elementary multiplier comparison.

nodes.title: Gamma asymptotics and numerical coefficient
nodes.notes: The manuscript derives the asymptotic using Stirling but states the decimal enclosure without a derivation. Accordingly this combined node has a thin border; the separate asymptotic node records the supplied derivation. Lean uses Euler’s Gamma limit and exact rational arithmetic.
nodes.statement_tex: The Gamma expression satisfies $G(a)=\frac{3}{2\Gamma(4/3)}a^{4/3}(1+o(1))$, hence the same asymptotic lower bound holds for $P_\tau(a,a)$. Its coefficient lies strictly between $1.67976$ and $1.67977$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Combine the exact lower bound with the Gamma-ratio limit and the independently certified rational enclosure.

nodes.title: Elementary four-thirds growth
nodes.notes: The concrete polynomial-value bound is proved for every positive integer a, without Gamma-function estimates.
nodes.statement_tex: For the manuscript function $P(a,b)=V_\tau(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})^{1/\tau}$ with admissible $\tau$ and every $a\ge1$, $P(a,a)\ge a^{4/3}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Start from $P(1,1)=1$. The recurrence multiplier is at least $(1+1/(3a))(1+1/a)\ge(1+1/a)^{4/3}$. Alternatively cube the desired multiplier comparison and prove a polynomial inequality; induction gives $a^4\le P(a,a)^3$, and monotonicity converts it to the real-power statement.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The elementary recurrence comparison and induction are now in the proof of Lemma 6.1.

nodes.title: Comparison of real powers
nodes.notes: The all-positive-integer formulation supplies the numerical comparison used by the elementary main proof.
nodes.statement_tex: If $r\in\mathbb R$ and $n^r\le2n$ for every positive integer $n$, then $r\le1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: If $r>1$, choose an integer $n>2^{1/(r-1)}$. Monotonicity of real powers implies $n^{r-1}>2$, contradicting $n^r\le2n$. This checked argument avoids limits.

nodes.title: Matrix multiplication exponent over every field
nodes.notes: Checked as a closed theorem for an arbitrary type K with only a Field K instance. There are no characteristic, cardinality, value-functional, or unproved growth assumptions.
nodes.statement_tex: For every field $F$, $\omega_F\le\frac94$. The only algebraic hypothesis is that $F$ is a field.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Take $\tau=\omega_F/3$, which is admissible because $\omega_F\ge2$. The concrete polynomial value satisfies all numerical growth hypotheses. Its elementary growth bound and the uniform upper bound give $a^{4\omega_F/9}\le V_{\omega_F/3}(\mathrm{PM}_{a,a})\le2a-1$ for every $a\ge1$. The checked numerical endpoint theorem yields $\omega_F\le9/4$. The exact rank formula and the Gamma-function sharpening are not required.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Local comparison of exponents in the proof of the main theorem.

nodes.title: Introduction: matrix multiplication scaling
nodes.notes: The library theorem holds for every real parameter, including infinite values.
nodes.statement_tex: For $2\le3\tau\le\omega$ and positive $\ell,m,n$, $V_\tau(T\otimes\langle\ell,m,n\rangle)=(\ell mn)^\tau V_\tau(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply matrix-block scaling and Kronecker commutativity to place the matrix factor on the right.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Introduction restatement of property (6) of the value-calculus lemma.

nodes.title: Introduction: value upper bound
nodes.notes: This introduction restatement is covered by the checked rank-value corollary.
nodes.statement_tex: For $2\le3\tau\le\omega$, $V_\tau(T)\le\widetilde R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: This is the introduction's restatement of the rank-value corollary.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Introduction restatement proved later in lem:rank-value.

nodes.title: Introduction: partial-sum inequality
nodes.notes: Checked by the same unconditional finite-family theorem as Lemma 4.12.
nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$, $V_\tau(\mathop{\diamondplus}_hT_h)^{1/\tau}\ge\sum_hV_\tau(T_h)^{1/\tau}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: This is the introduction's restatement of partial-sum superadditivity.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Introduction restatement proved later in lem:value-diamondsum.

nodes.title: Implemented coefficient tensor API
nodes.notes: Checked coordinate arrays and factor-map actions. Finite families, powers, and permutation/reindexing laws are checked in their dedicated support nodes.
nodes.statement_tex: Coefficient tensors, factor-map actions, restrictions, mutual-restriction equivalence, Kronecker products, binary direct sums, and binary partial sums are defined. Factor maps compose; restriction and equivalence have their expected reflexivity and transitivity laws.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The checked implementation uses finite sums for the factor-map action. Reorder the six sums to prove map composition; use identity matrices for reflexivity and composed witnesses for transitivity.

nodes.title: Implemented diagonal and multiplication tensors
nodes.notes: Checked coordinate definitions only; no rank identities or bilinear-structure equivalences are claimed.
nodes.statement_tex: The diagonal tensor, matrix multiplication tensor, and polynomial multiplication tensor are defined by their coefficient formulas on finite index sets.

nodes.title: Binary partial-sum projections
nodes.notes: This proves item 1 of diamondplus-basic in the binary implementation, not all six items.
nodes.statement_tex: For two tensors with the same first index set, their binary partial sum restricts to either summand using the identity map on the first factor.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use identity matrices on the first factor and the coordinate projections on the second and third factors.

nodes.title: Implemented numerical growth hypotheses
nodes.notes: Checked in Omega/Analysis/Growth.lean. This is a structure of hypotheses, not an axiom asserting their existence for polynomial multiplication value.
nodes.statement_tex: For $P:\mathbb N\times\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$, the growth hypotheses assert symmetry on positive indices, $P(1,a)=a$, the concavity inequality $pP(a,b)+P(a,b+p+1)\le(p+1)P(a,b+1)$ for $a,b\ge1$ and $p\ge0$, and $3P(a,a)\le P(a,4a-1)$ for $a\ge1$.

nodes.title: Checked abstract diagonal recurrence
nodes.notes: The generic numerical theorem is checked. Its application to the manuscript P depends on aux:polynomial-value-hypotheses.
nodes.statement_tex: If $P$ satisfies the numerical growth hypotheses, then for every $a\ge1$, $\frac{(3a+1)(3a+2)}{3a(3a-1)}P(a,a)\le P(a+1,a+1)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply concavity twice at the parameters used in the manuscript, then use tripling and symmetry. The checked proof clears positive denominators and combines the resulting inequalities.

nodes.title: Checked abstract four-thirds growth
nodes.statement_tex: If $P$ satisfies the numerical growth hypotheses and $a\ge1$, then $P(a,a)\ge a^{4/3}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: A polynomial identity proves the cubed recurrence-factor inequality. Inductively obtain $0\le P(a,a)$ and $a^4\le P(a,a)^3$, then apply monotonicity of real powers.

nodes.title: Checked numerical nine-quarters conclusion
nodes.notes: This generic numerical implication is checked independently. The concrete polynomial-value hypotheses and upper bound are now supplied, and the final field-uniform theorem applies it without additional assumptions.
nodes.statement_tex: Suppose $P$ satisfies the numerical growth hypotheses, $w>0$, and $P(a,a)^{w/3}\le2a-1$ for every positive integer $a$. Then $w\le9/4$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Raise the elementary lower bound to $w/3$ and combine it with the assumed upper bound. The power-comparison lemma gives $4w/9\le1$.

nodes.title: Implemented polynomial degeneration witnesses
nodes.notes: Checked polynomial definition and elementary properties. Composition and operation compatibility are checked in their support node; equivalence with rational-function specialization is proved in aux:rational-degeneration-equivalence.
nodes.statement_tex: A polynomial degeneration witness records three polynomial factor maps, an order $d$, and a remainder, whose transformed tensor is $X^dS+X^{d+1}E$. Restriction gives an order-zero witness, degeneration is reflexive, the order coefficient is $S$, and all lower coefficients vanish. The zero tensor degenerates only to zero.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use constant polynomial matrices for restriction. Extract coefficients from the witness identity, using the vanishing of coefficients below the displayed powers.

nodes.title: Implemented ordinary rank and monotonicity
nodes.statement_tex: Tensor rank is the least $r$ such that $\langle r\rangle$ restricts to $T$. The minimum exists, is attained, and is monotone under restriction and invariant under equivalence and reindexing. A tensor has rank zero exactly when it is zero, and a pure tensor has rank at most one.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The coordinate expansion gives a restriction of a finite diagonal tensor. Define rank by the least such natural number, then use composition of restrictions and minimality. Prove the zero and pure-tensor cases by explicit maps.

nodes.title: Implemented asymptotic rank definition
nodes.notes: The infimum definition and elementary bounds are checked here. Rank-root convergence, degeneration monotonicity, and the other asymptotic-rank operation laws are checked in separate support nodes.
nodes.statement_tex: Kronecker powers are indexed by finite tuples. Define $\widetilde R(T)=\inf_{n\ge1}R(T^{\otimes n})^{1/n}$. The set of rank roots is nonempty and bounded below by zero, so $0\le\widetilde R(T)\le R(T^{\otimes n})^{1/n}$ for $n\ge1$. In particular $\widetilde R(T)\le R(T)$ and $\widetilde R(0)=0$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use the first tensor power for nonemptiness and the upper bound by ordinary rank. Real powers of nonnegative ranks provide the lower bound for the infimum.

nodes.title: Rank bounds for sums and products
nodes.notes: Checked over every commutative semiring; these are ordinary-rank bounds.
nodes.statement_tex: A rank-minimizing diagonal restriction gives a decomposition into pure tensors. Rank is subadditive for finite sums in common spaces and for ordinary direct sums, submultiplicative for Kronecker products, and cannot increase under factor maps.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Concatenate pure-tensor decompositions for addition and multiply their terms for Kronecker products. For direct sums, embed each summand with zero padding and apply subadditivity.

nodes.title: Restrictions and binary tensor operations
nodes.statement_tex: Factor maps commute with Kronecker products and ordinary direct sums. Consequently restriction respects both operations, and zero padding a tensor is a restriction.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use Kronecker products of the factor matrices for tensor products and block-diagonal matrices for direct sums. Expand the finite coordinate sums.

nodes.title: Tensor-power identities and rank bounds
nodes.statement_tex: Splitting finite tuples identifies $T^{\otimes(m+n)}$ with $T^{\otimes m}\otimes T^{\otimes n}$. Hence $R(T^{\otimes(m+n)})\le R(T^{\otimes m})R(T^{\otimes n})$ and $R(T^{\otimes n})\le R(T)^n$. The zeroth power has rank at most one.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Reindex by concatenation and splitting of finite tuples, use invariance of rank under reindexing, and apply the binary product bound. Induct for the bound by $R(T)^n$.

nodes.title: Composition and operations for polynomial degeneration
nodes.notes: All witness constructions are checked over commutative semirings. Over fields the polynomial relation agrees with rational-function specialization by aux:rational-degeneration-equivalence.
nodes.statement_tex: Polynomial degeneration is transitive and respects tensor powers, binary Kronecker products, and ordinary direct sums. A witness of order $d$ gives a witness of order $dn$ for the $n$th tensor powers. Binary product witnesses have order $d+e$; scalar shifts align direct-sum orders.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: For composition with a witness of order $e$, substitute $X^{e+1}$ in the first witness before composing factor maps. Expand products with their remainders. For direct sums, shift orders to a common value and use block-diagonal maps.

nodes.title: Rank bound for polynomial coefficient extraction
nodes.notes: Uses formal coefficients only, with no interpolation or assumption that the coefficient field is infinite.
nodes.statement_tex: The coefficient of order $d$ of a polynomial restriction is a sum of $\binom{d+2}{2}$ ordinary restrictions, so its rank is at most $\binom{d+2}{2}R(T)$. A witness of order $d$ gives $R(S^{\otimes N})\le\binom{dN+2}{2}R(T^{\otimes N})$. The coarser quadratic bounds remain available.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Expand into two antidiagonal sums and count their total cardinality exactly. Apply rank subadditivity and restriction monotonicity, then apply the same estimate to the tensor-power witness.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The proof of Lemma 2.2 explicitly counts exponent triples and obtains the binomial bound.

nodes.title: Polynomial overhead disappears in rank-root limits
nodes.statement_tex: For fixed nonnegative integers $d,k$, $((dn+1)^k)^{1/n}\to1$. If nonnegative submultiplicative real sequences satisfy $v_n\le(dn+1)^ku_n$ for $n\ge1$, then their rank-root limits satisfy $\lim v_n^{1/n}\le\lim u_n^{1/n}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use the real-power asymptotic limit for an affine function, then a fixed integer power. Apply the submultiplicative-sequence limit theorem and take limits in the root inequality.

nodes.title: Asymptotic rank is the limit of rank roots
nodes.statement_tex: The infimum defining asymptotic rank equals the limit: $\widetilde R(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}R(T^{\otimes n})^{1/n}$. In particular, a bound $R(S^{\otimes n})\le(dn+1)^kR(T^{\otimes n})$ for all $n\ge1$ implies $\widetilde R(S)\le\widetilde R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Identify the defining infimum with the limit in mathlib for a nonnegative submultiplicative sequence. Apply the polynomial-overhead comparison theorem to the two rank sequences.

nodes.title: Degeneration cannot increase asymptotic rank
nodes.notes: Checked for the polynomial-witness relation over all commutative semirings, hence over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: If $T\trianglerighteq S$, then $\widetilde R(S)\le\widetilde R(T)$. More explicitly, a polynomial witness of order $d$ gives $R(S^{\otimes n})\le(dn+1)^2R(T^{\otimes n})$ for every $n\ge0$. Asymptotic rank is therefore also monotone under restriction and invariant under equivalence.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Take tensor powers of the witness, whose order becomes $dn$, and extract its leading coefficient. Apply the coefficient-rank bound and then remove the polynomial overhead in the rank-root limit.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The revised Lemma 2.2 supplies the coefficient-extraction proof and its border-rank consequence.

nodes.title: Border rank and its asymptotic lower bound
nodes.notes: Border rank uses polynomial witnesses, proved equivalent to rational-function degeneration. The subrank variants are checked in the separate subrank-invariants node.
nodes.statement_tex: Border rank is the least size of a diagonal tensor degenerating to $T$, and this minimum is attained. It is monotone under degeneration and satisfies $\widetilde R(T)\le\underline R(T)\le R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: An ordinary rank decomposition supplies a diagonal degeneration source. Take the least such size, use transitivity for border-rank monotonicity, and apply asymptotic-rank monotonicity to a minimizing source.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The revised Lemma 2.2 supplies the coefficient-extraction proof and its border-rank consequence.

nodes.title: Implemented matrix multiplication and exponent definitions
nodes.notes: The coordinate tensor and rank-based exponent are checked. The special-shape equivalences are checked in the full matrix-multiplication definition node, and the bilinear interpretation has its own correspondence node.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive integers $\ell,m,n$, define $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k}e_{ij}\otimes e_{jk}\otimes e_{ik}$. For every field $F$, set $\omega_F=\log_2\widetilde R_F(\langle2,2,2\rangle)$.

nodes.title: Matrix rank of a Kronecker product
nodes.notes: No characteristic or field-cardinality hypothesis is used; rectangular and empty shapes are included.
nodes.statement_tex: For arbitrary finite rectangular matrices $A,B$ over a field, $\operatorname{rank}(A\otimes B)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\operatorname{rank}(B)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Identify the Kronecker matrix map with the tensor product of the two matrix maps using finite-function coordinate equivalences. The image is the tensor product of their images, whose dimensions multiply.

nodes.title: Implemented flattenings and their product ranks
nodes.notes: The Lean factor indices 0, 1, 2 correspond to the paper indices 1, 2, 3. Restriction and degeneration monotonicity are tracked separately in the full flattening-calculus node.
nodes.statement_tex: Each tensor has three flattening matrices, with one factor indexing columns and the other two indexing rows. For each factor $i$, $R^{(i)}(T)\le R(T)$. These ranks are invariant under coordinate reindexing and satisfy $R^{(i)}(T\otimes S)=R^{(i)}(T)R^{(i)}(S)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: A rank decomposition factors each flattening through a space of dimension $R(T)$. A tensor-product flattening is a coordinate reindexing of the matrix Kronecker product, so its rank is given by matrix-rank multiplicativity.

nodes.title: Flattening ranks of tensor powers
nodes.statement_tex: For every $n\ge0$ and each factor $i$, $R^{(i)}(T^{\otimes n})=R^{(i)}(T)^n$. In particular, every flattening of the zeroth power has rank one, including when a factor of $T$ has dimension zero.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: At power zero the coordinate types are singleton types, giving a rank-one matrix. At power one remove singleton tuples. For the induction step split tuples, use invariance under reindexing, and apply the binary product identity.

nodes.title: Exact rank invariants of diagonal tensors
nodes.notes: Checked over every field, including r = 0. Border rank uses the implemented polynomial-witness definition.
nodes.statement_tex: For every integer $r\ge0$, all three flattening ranks of $\langle r\rangle$ equal $r$, and $R(\langle r\rangle)=\underline R(\langle r\rangle)=\widetilde R(\langle r\rangle)=r$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Select the diagonal rows of each flattening to obtain an identity submatrix. The resulting lower bounds match the elementary upper bound on the rank of a diagonal tensor.

nodes.title: First flattening rank of matrix multiplication
nodes.notes: This node proves the first flattening formula; no formulas for the other two matrix-multiplication flattenings are asserted here.
nodes.statement_tex: For integers $\ell,m\ge0$ and $n\ge1$, the first flattening of $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle$ has rank $\ell m$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Fix one index in the nonempty third matrix dimension. The corresponding rows give an identity submatrix of size $\ell m$, matching the number of columns.

nodes.title: The lower bound two for the exponent
nodes.notes: Only the field assumption is required. The upper bound is also checked in the full omega-bounds node.
nodes.statement_tex: For every field $F$, $\widetilde R_F(\langle2,2,2\rangle)\ge4$, hence $\omega_F\ge2$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply the first-flattening lower bound to the two-by-two matrix-multiplication tensor, whose first flattening has rank four. The base-two logarithm is increasing on positive reals.

nodes.title: Asymptotic rank of powers and products
nodes.notes: Checked including power zero. The power law holds over nontrivial commutative semirings; the product bound holds over arbitrary commutative semirings.
nodes.statement_tex: Over every field, $\widetilde R(T^{\otimes k})=\widetilde R(T)^k$ for all integers $k\ge0$, and $\widetilde R(T\otimes S)\le\widetilde R(T)\widetilde R(S)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Regroup power coordinates explicitly. For $k>0$, apply the root-limit theorem along the subsequence $Nk$; handle the empty power separately. For products, take limits in the ordinary rank product bound.

nodes.title: Asymptotic rank of sums
nodes.notes: Checked over arbitrary commutative semirings, including zero tensors. Uniform exponential bounds include the zeroth power; the limiting argument uses positive powers.
nodes.statement_tex: Asymptotic rank is subadditive: $\widetilde R(T\oplus S)\le\widetilde R(T)+\widetilde R(S)$. For tensors with the same coordinate sets, also $\widetilde R(T+S)\le\widetilde R(T)+\widetilde R(S)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: For rates $a>\widetilde R(T)$ and $b>\widetilde R(S)$, bound every power rank by $C_Ta^k$ and $C_Sb^k$. Expand a power of $T+S$ over subsets of its coordinates and separate each subset from its complement. The resulting sum is bounded by $C_TC_S(a+b)^N$. Take roots and limits, then let the rates decrease. Obtain direct sums by embedding into disjoint coordinate blocks.

nodes.title: Matrix multiplication dimension calculus
nodes.notes: Checked for all natural matrix dimensions and powers, including zero. Coordinate restrictions and equivalences use commutative semirings; scalar asymptotic-rank normalization is stated over fields. The three special-shape presentations are checked in Definition 2.4.
nodes.statement_tex: Decreasing matrix dimensions gives a restriction. Moreover, $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle\otimes\langle\ell',m',n'\rangle\cong\langle\ell\ell',mm',nn'\rangle$ and $\langle\ell,m,n\rangle^{\otimes k}\cong\langle\ell^k,m^k,n^k\rangle$. The elementary bound is $R(\langle\ell,m,n\rangle)\le\ell mn$, and $\widetilde R(\langle1,1,1\rangle)=1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use coordinate inclusions for restrictions, finite-product and tuple equivalences for products and powers, and the defining sum of pure tensors for the rank bound. Identify scalar multiplication with the diagonal tensor of size one.

nodes.title: Monotone functions preserving powers
nodes.notes: Checked general analytic helper. Monotonicity and f(1)=1 ensure all logarithms at positive integer arguments are defined. No lower bound greater than one on f(2) is required.
nodes.statement_tex: Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be monotone, satisfy $f(1)=1$, and preserve natural powers: $f(a^k)=f(a)^k$. Then $f(n)=n^{\log_2 f(2)}$ for every $n\ge1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Compare $a^k$ with $b^{\lceil\log_b(a^k)\rceil}$ for $a\ge1$ and $b\ge2$. Taking logarithms bounds $k\log f(a)$ by $k\log_b(a)\log f(b)$ plus a fixed rounding error. The Archimedean property removes that error. Interchange the two bases to get equality, and handle $n=1$ directly.

nodes.title: Repeated direct-sum blocks
nodes.notes: Checked including zero copies and zeroth powers for the power identities and upper bound. Block projection requires a positive number of copies. The coefficient lemma verifies that the diagonal-product representation is exactly the ordinary repeated direct sum.
nodes.statement_tex: The ordinary direct sum of $a$ identical tensors is represented by $T^{\oplus a}=\langle a\rangle\otimes T$, with coefficients zero unless the three block labels agree. Its powers satisfy $(T^{\oplus a})^{\otimes n}\cong(T^{\otimes n})^{\oplus a^n}$. Over a field, $\widetilde R(T^{\oplus a})\le a\widetilde R(T)$; when $a\ge1$, selecting one block gives the reverse lower bound $\widetilde R(T)\le\widetilde R(T^{\oplus a})$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Encode words of block labels as a single finite label and split tuples of block-and-basis indices. Projection to one block is a restriction. The upper bound follows from product submultiplicativity and the normalization $\widetilde R(\langle a\rangle)=a$.

nodes.title: Matrix multiplication capacity comparison
nodes.notes: Checked over every field. The exponents n,m and copy count a may be zero; only the matrix dimension b must be positive. The auxiliary diagonal restriction and rank-attainment lemmas work over commutative semirings.
nodes.statement_tex: Fix $b\ge1$ and put $q=\widetilde R(\langle2,2,2\rangle)$ and $s=\widetilde R(\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a})$. For natural $n,m$, if $R(\langle2,2,2\rangle^{\otimes n})\le a^m$, then $q^n(b^\omega)^m\le s^m$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: A rank bound gives a restriction from the diagonal tensor of size $a^m$. Tensor it with $\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\otimes m}$ and identify the source as the $m$th power of the repeated block tensor. Matrix dimensions multiply under tensor products, so the square-size identity computes the target asymptotic rank exactly. Apply restriction monotonicity and power multiplicativity.

nodes.title: Integer capacities and root growth
nodes.notes: Checked analytic helper with all logarithm and division hypotheses explicit. The ceiling is implemented as Nat.clog, so every exponent is an integer. The limit ignores n=0.
nodes.statement_tex: Let $r_n\ge1$ be natural numbers with $r_n^{1/n}\to q>1$, let $a\ge2$ be an integer, and let $p\ge1$. If $r_n\le a^m$ always implies $q^n\le p^m$, then $a\le p$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Take $m=\lceil\log_a r_n\rceil$. Taking logarithms of the capacity inequality and using the ceiling bound gives $\log q\le(\log(r_n^{1/n})/\log a+1/n)\log p$ for positive $n$. Pass to the limit and cancel the positive logarithms of $a$ and $q$.

nodes.title: Permuting the three tensor factors
nodes.notes: Checked over commutative semirings. The S3 interface permutes the coordinate types as well as the coefficients; its six-case representation is proved bijective to Equiv.Perm (Fin 3).
nodes.statement_tex: The six permutations of three tensor factors preserve ordinary rank and asymptotic rank. A three-cycle and a transposition generate the six explicit orders, identified bijectively with $\mathfrak S_3$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Permute each pure tensor in an attained rank decomposition to obtain one rank inequality; apply the inverse permutation for the other. Tensor powers commute with these permutations, so the asymptotic-rank equality follows from its definition. Enumerate the six orders and identify them with permutations of three slots.

nodes.title: Asymptotic rank of symmetrization
nodes.notes: Checked over every commutative semiring, including zero tensors. This estimate does not use any fractional-value identity.
nodes.statement_tex: For every tensor over a field, $\widetilde R(T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3})\le\widetilde R(T)^6$. The cyclic product of three rotations has asymptotic rank at most $\widetilde R(T)^3$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Apply product submultiplicativity to the three even and three odd permutations, using permutation invariance of asymptotic rank.

nodes.title: Matrices as tensors with a unit factor
nodes.notes: Checked over every field. This supplies an algebraic route to flattening monotonicity without a separate minors or algebraic-closure argument.
nodes.statement_tex: Regard a matrix $A$ as a three-tensor with one unit factor. Its ordinary tensor rank and asymptotic rank both equal the matrix rank of $A$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Choose a basis of the image to decompose the matrix into exactly its rank many outer products. This gives the tensor-rank upper bound; the first flattening recovers the original matrix and gives the matching asymptotic lower bound.

nodes.title: Flattening monotonicity under polynomial degeneration
nodes.notes: Checked over every field. The rational/polynomial degeneration equivalence transfers this result to the manuscript relation.
nodes.statement_tex: For the polynomial degeneration relation, $T\trianglerighteq S$ implies $R_i(S)\le R_i(T)$ for each of the three flattenings. Flattening rank is also monotone under restriction and invariant under tensor equivalence.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Group the two complementary factor maps by their matrix Kronecker product, transporting the original polynomial witness to the corresponding matrix tensors without changing its order. Apply asymptotic-rank monotonicity and the equality of matrix-tensor asymptotic rank with matrix rank.

nodes.title: Flattening ranks of repeated blocks
nodes.notes: Checked over every field, including zero copies. Only the displayed square-matrix specialization requires a positive matrix dimension.
nodes.statement_tex: For each flattening, $R_i(T^{\oplus a})=aR_i(T)$. In particular, the first flattening of $\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a}$ has rank $ab^2$ when $b\ge1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use the diagonal-product description of repeated blocks, flattening-rank multiplicativity, diagonal normalization, and the matrix-multiplication flattening formula.

nodes.title: Nonzero tensors supply the unit
nodes.notes: Checked over every field. No nonemptiness assumption on coordinate types is imposed; it follows from a nonzero coefficient when required.
nodes.statement_tex: Every nonzero tensor over a field restricts to $\langle1\rangle$, hence has asymptotic rank at least one. Products and powers of nonzero tensors are nonzero, including the zeroth power.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Select one nonzero coefficient and rescale by its inverse. Products use products of nonzero coefficients; powers use constant index tuples. Apply asymptotic-rank monotonicity for the lower bound.

nodes.title: Implemented fractional value and positive witnesses
nodes.notes: The supremum formula holds definitionally for every tensor. The zero witness type is proved empty, giving value zero by the empty-supremum law. Scores and values extend to all real parameters; the paper uses positive parameters. The rational-value-equivalence node identifies the same supremum with rational-function witnesses.
nodes.statement_tex: A witness consists of positive integers $a,b,c,d,N$ and $\langle d,d,d\rangle^{\oplus c}\otimes(T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3})^{\otimes N}\trianglerighteq\langle b,b,b\rangle^{\oplus a}$. Its positive score is $(ab^{3\tau}/(cd^{3\tau}))^{1/(6N)}$. Define the value as the supremum of all witness scores in $[0,+\infty]$. Every witness forces $T\ne0$; therefore the zero tensor has value zero as the empty supremum.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Store the positive sizes and degeneration as a witness structure. A zero source cannot degenerate to the nonzero target of a positive witness, so the witness type for the zero tensor is empty. Define value by the indexed supremum of the extended nonnegative real scores; the empty-supremum identity proves the zero case. Each witness bounds the supremum without a separate nonzero hypothesis.

nodes.title: Bounding intermediate witness scores
nodes.notes: Checked without logarithms or division by w-2. The degenerate interval w=2 and zero right-hand rate are included; no value calculus is assumed.
nodes.statement_tex: For positive real $a,b,c,d$, a natural $k\ge1$, and $R\ge0$, suppose $ab^2\le cd^2R^k$ and $ab^w\le cd^wR^k$. Then $(ab^t/(cd^t))^{1/k}\le R$ for every $2\le t\le w$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The ratio equals $(a/c)(b/d)^t$. If $b\le d$, the lower exponent controls the ratio; if $d\le b$, the upper exponent does. Apply monotonicity of the positive root to the appropriate bound.

nodes.title: A score-one witness for nonzero tensors
nodes.notes: Checked over every field, with no admissible-interval assumption. Nonemptiness is established before any manipulation of the supremum.
nodes.statement_tex: Every nonzero tensor has a fractional-value witness with $a=b=c=d=N=1$, whose score is one for every real $\tau$. Thus its witness set is nonempty and its polynomial-witness value is at least one.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The six-factor symmetrization is nonzero. Tensoring it with the scalar matrix-multiplication block remains nonzero, so it restricts to the unit diagonal and then to the target scalar block. This restriction is a degeneration and gives the all-one witness.

nodes.title: Rational specialization and polynomial witnesses
nodes.notes: Checked without assumptions on characteristic, field cardinality, or nonzero tensors. Regularity uses the reduced rational-function denominator, so removable poles are handled correctly.
nodes.statement_tex: For finite-dimensional tensors over every field, rational-function specialization is equivalent to polynomial degeneration witnesses. The rational factor maps may have poles at zero; their transformed tensor must be regular there and specialize to the target.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: In one direction divide a factor map by $X^d$, obtaining the regular output $S+XE$. Conversely clear the finite factor denominators and a separate common denominator of the regular output. Extract the common power of $X$ from the factor denominator product, normalize the remaining constant term, and use polynomial division by $X$ for the remainder.

nodes.title: Witness transport along symmetrized degeneration
nodes.notes: Witness transport under degeneration of symmetrizations proves value monotonicity and permutation invariance. This supports the updated direct argument in the manuscript. The value may be infinite, and the parameter need not lie in the admissible interval.
nodes.statement_tex: If $T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3}\trianglerighteq S^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3}$, every witness for $S$ is a witness for $T$ with the same parameters and score. Hence $V_\tau(S)\le V_\tau(T)$ for every real $\tau$. Value is invariant under all six factor permutations. A zero tensor has no positive witness, so the defining supremum also handles zero without a separate branch.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Permute polynomial factor maps to transport degeneration through symmetrization. Compose a powered symmetrized degeneration with each witness and take the extended-real supremum. Apply the strengthened monotonicity in both directions to the symmetrization equivalences for factor permutations.

nodes.title: Equality with the rational-function value supremum
nodes.notes: This closes the correspondence obligation for Definition 4.3, rather than merely identifying the two degeneration relations.
nodes.statement_tex: The polynomial and rational-function value witnesses are equivalent with identical integer parameters and scores. Their extended-real suprema are equal for every tensor and every real parameter, including the zero tensor.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Transfer the degeneration field of each witness using the rational/polynomial equivalence. The score expression is unchanged. Compare the two indexed suprema using these transports in both directions; the zero case follows from the absence of a positive witness.

nodes.title: Witness products and exact power laws
nodes.notes: Zero tensors and infinite values are included. Only the zero-power case requires the admissible parameter interval.
nodes.statement_tex: Cross-powering two witnesses gives a product witness whose score is the product of their scores. Transporting witnesses into and out of positive tensor powers gives $V_\tau(T\otimes S)\ge V_\tau(T)V_\tau(S)$ and $V_\tau(T^{\otimes n})=V_\tau(T)^n$ for $n\ge1$, for every real $\tau$. The power-zero identity holds in the admissible interval.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use explicit finite coordinate equivalences to rearrange products, iterated powers, and matrix blocks. For witnesses of orders $N,M$, take powers $M,N$ to obtain a common order $NM$. Prove the score identities via their logarithms, then distribute extended-real products and positive powers over suprema. Handle power zero by unit normalization.

nodes.title: Absorbing matrix blocks into value witnesses
nodes.notes: Checked for every real parameter, every tensor, and infinite values. Diagonal multiplicity may be zero; matrix dimensions are positive, as in the manuscript definition.
nodes.statement_tex: If $S^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3}\cong\langle q,q,q\rangle^{\oplus r}\otimes T^{\otimes\mathfrak S_3}$ with $r,q\ge1$, then $V_\tau(S)=r^{1/6}q^{\tau/2}V_\tau(T)$. Consequently diagonal and matrix-multiplication factors obey the two exact scaling laws in Lemma 4.6.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: For a witness of order $N$, stripping the block multiplies its denominator sizes by $r^N,q^N$. Adding the block multiplies its numerator sizes by the same factors. Their scores differ by $r^{1/6}q^{\tau/2}$. Take suprema in both directions, then apply the diagonal and matrix-multiplication symmetrization formulas.

nodes.title: Uniform degeneration to polynomial multiplication
nodes.notes: The uniform degeneration part of Lemma 2.6 is checked, including zero input sizes. For positive input sizes, the exact border/asymptotic ranks and the ordinary-rank estimates are checked in their separate correspondence nodes.
nodes.statement_tex: Over every field, $\langle a+b-1\rangle\trianglerighteq\mathrm{PM}_{a,b}$. More generally, distinct interpolation nodes give an explicit restriction from the diagonal over the field containing those nodes.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Evaluate at distinct nodes and extract coefficients from the Lagrange basis. Over the rational function field use $1,X,\ldots,X^{a+b-2}$, whose distinctness follows from polynomial degree. The output is exactly the constant polynomial-multiplication tensor, hence regular at zero. Apply the rational/polynomial degeneration equivalence.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.6: exact border and asymptotic ranks
nodes.notes: This node isolates the checked field-uniform part of Lemma 2.6. Both input sizes must be positive; the formula does not extend to empty inputs. The separate ordinary-rank upper bounds are not claimed here.
nodes.statement_tex: For every field $F$ and $a,b\ge1$, the third flattening of $\mathrm{PM}_{a,b}$ has rank $a+b-1$. Consequently, $R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})\ge a+b-1$ and $\underline R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})=\widetilde R(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})=a+b-1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: For each output degree $k$, select the input pair $(\min(k,a-1),k-\min(k,a-1))$. These rows form an identity submatrix in the third flattening. Its rank bounds ordinary, border, and asymptotic rank from below. The diagonal degeneration gives border rank at most $a+b-1$, and $\widetilde R\le\underline R$ gives the asymptotic upper bound. This proves both identities without another finite-extension argument.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: The third-flattening lower bound and the two exact rank identities are proved within Lemma 2.6; this node isolates its checked field-uniform claims.

nodes.title: Finite dependent tensor products and value bounds
nodes.notes: The tensor identities hold over commutative semirings; the value inequality holds over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: Finite tensor products may have dependent coordinate spaces. Reindexing their factors gives a coordinate equivalence. In the admissible interval, their fractional value is at least the product of the factor values, including the empty product.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Group coordinates into dependent function spaces. Prove invariance by reindexing the finite coefficient product. Split a finite product into its first factor and the remaining factors; use product supermultiplicativity inductively and unit normalization for the empty product.

nodes.title: Monomial weights on coordinate pullbacks
nodes.notes: The helper allows repeated selected coordinates and does not impose characteristic or field-size assumptions.
nodes.statement_tex: Assign nonnegative integer weights to the three factor maps of a coordinate pullback. If every supported coefficient has total weight at least $d$, the terms of weight exactly $d$ form a degeneration target.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use polynomial factor matrices with one selected coordinate per row and a monomial scalar. Divide the transformed tensor by the common power $X^d$ coefficientwise, separate its constant term, and record the remaining terms in the polynomial remainder.

nodes.title: Independent maps in ordinary direct sums
nodes.notes: These independent block maps are used only after separation. No analogous unconstrained congruence is asserted for partially direct sums.
nodes.statement_tex: Ordinary direct sums of dependent families respect independent restrictions and equivalences in every block. A direct sum of $Q$ blocks equivalent to a common tensor is equivalent to $Q$ copies of that tensor.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Place each block factor map on the diagonal of the corresponding family matrix. Off-diagonal block tags give zero coefficients. Reindex a constant family by the finite cardinality to identify it with repeated copies.

nodes.title: Words with prescribed counts
nodes.notes: Zero counts, length zero, and empty alphabets are included.
nodes.statement_tex: Words of length $N$ with symbol counts $c_h$ exist exactly when $\sum_h c_h=N$. When this equality holds, their number is $\binom{N}{(c_h)_h}$, and any two such words differ by a permutation of their positions.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Construct a permutation from bijections of the symbol fibers. Apply orbit--stabilizer to the action of position permutations: the stabilizer has size $\prod_h c_h!$, while the full permutation group has size $N!$.

nodes.title: Grouping tensor products by symbol counts
nodes.notes: The explicit coordinate identifications include zero counts and empty products. They are applied separately to ordinary-direct-sum blocks after separation.
nodes.statement_tex: The tensor product along a word with counts $c_h$ is coordinate-isomorphic to $\bigotimes_h T_h^{\otimes c_h}$. All three coordinate types may depend on the symbol.
