nodes.proof_plan_tex: Split positions into fibers of the word and enumerate each fiber by its count. The resulting dependent coordinate equivalences group the coefficient product into the corresponding tensor powers.

nodes.title: Selecting words from powers of partial sums
nodes.notes: This proves the needed selection directly, without assuming that independent first-factor equivalences preserve partial sums.
nodes.statement_tex: A power of a partial direct sum restricts to the partial sum of tensor products indexed by any selected family of distinct block words, with its first factor still shared.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Pull back the second and third coordinate functions along the selected words and leave the first coordinate unchanged. Distinct words differ at some position, making the cross-block coefficient vanish.

nodes.title: From all type bounds to a sum bound
nodes.notes: Zero weights and empty families are allowed. This replaces the entropy asymptotic and rational approximation on the main proof path.
nodes.statement_tex: For nonnegative $a_h,B$ and $C>0$, suppose every count vector of total $N\ge1$ satisfies $\binom{N}{(c_h)_h}\prod_h a_h^{c_h}\le C B^N$. Then $\sum_h a_h\le B$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Expand $(\sum_h a_h)^N$ by the multinomial theorem and sum the individual bounds. The count vectors inject into $[0,N]^H$, so there are at most $(N+1)^{|H|}$. Take $N$-th roots; the polynomial factor and the fixed positive constant both tend to one.

nodes.title: Weighted AM--GM form of the entropy bound
nodes.notes: This is the checked upper-bound half of the entropy variational identity. The attained maximum and equality are checked separately in the manuscript lemma node.
nodes.statement_tex: For a probability vector $q$ and nonnegative $a_h$, $2^{H(q)}\prod_h a_h^{q_h}\le\sum_h a_h$. For $\tau>0$, this gives $2^{\tau H(q)}\prod_h v_h^{q_h}\le(\sum_h v_h^{1/\tau})^\tau$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use weighted AM--GM on the positive support and the product formula for exponential entropy. Handle a positive probability at a zero base directly; zero probabilities use the convention $0^0=1$.

nodes.title: Coordinate models for polynomial multiplication
nodes.statement_tex: The repeated coefficient model $\mathrm{PM}^{[r]}_{a,b}$ has the literal shared first factor $F^a$ and equals $\mathrm{PM}_{a,b}\otimes\langle1,1,r\rangle$ up to canonical singleton-coordinate identifications. Swapping the inputs exchanges $a,b$, and $\mathrm{PM}_{1,b}$ is equivalent to $\langle1,1,b\rangle$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Give explicit coordinate bijections. Repeated copies retain the first input index; only the canonical one-dimensional matrix coordinate is inserted. The last-two-factor swap is also defined explicitly.

nodes.title: Degeneration from three split-map identities
nodes.notes: A checked coordinate criterion sufficient for polynomial multiplication. It does not claim the full abstract short-exact-sequence lemma.
nodes.statement_tex: If $\operatorname{map}(1,B_0,C_0)T=T_0$, $\operatorname{map}(1,B_0,C_1)T=0$, and $\operatorname{map}(1,B_1,C_1)T=T_1$, then $T\trianglerighteq T_0\diamondplus T_1$. The fourth block is unrestricted. This holds over every commutative semiring.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Combine the two second-factor maps and two third-factor maps into sum-indexed maps. Assign second-factor weights $(0,1)$ and third-factor weights $(1,0)$. At order one the two diagonal blocks survive, the zero block causes no lower term, and the fourth block has higher order.

nodes.title: Explicit maps on bivariate coefficient grids
nodes.statement_tex: On the rectangular coefficient grid, multiplication by $x-y$ is an adjacent-edge difference; $x^s\mapsto x^{\min(s,b-1)}y^{s-\min(s,b-1)}$ is a section of diagonal evaluation. Diagonal summation kills edge differences and diagonal-tail extraction recovers their coefficients.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Check the two endpoint indices and their degree bounds, then prove the diagonal and tail indicator identities. The cancellation uses only ring arithmetic, so it also holds in characteristic two.

nodes.title: Real-root value identities for binary partial sums
nodes.statement_tex: In the admissible interval, $V_\tau(T\diamondplus S)^{1/\tau}\ge V_\tau(T)^{1/\tau}+V_\tau(S)^{1/\tau}$, and $V_\tau(\mathrm{PM}^{[r]}_{a,b})^{1/\tau}=rV_\tau(\mathrm{PM}_{a,b})^{1/\tau}$ for $r\ge1$. Exchanging the last two factors preserves value, as does exchanging the two polynomial input sizes.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Transport the finite-family inequality through the two-element family equivalence while preserving the shared first coordinate. Apply rectangular matrix scaling and permutation invariance; admissible-interval finiteness justifies passing to real values.

nodes.title: Uniform upper bound for polynomial value
nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$, $P(a,b)^\tau\le a+b-1$ for positive $a,b$. In particular, $P(a,a)^\tau\le2a-1$ for every $a\ge1$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Cancel the positive reciprocal exponent in $P$. Bound fractional value by asymptotic rank, and use the diagonal-to-polynomial-multiplication degeneration. Only the upper bound is needed, not the exact rank formula.

nodes.title: Subrank maxima and asymptotic subrank supremum
nodes.notes: Definitions agree with Definition 2.1 over every field, including zero tensors and empty coordinate sets. Maxima are attained, and the real supremum is bounded; no convention for an unbounded supremum is used.
nodes.statement_tex: The maxima defining $Q(T)$ and $\underline Q(T)$ are attained, with $Q(T)\le\underline Q(T)\le\underline R(T)$. Restriction is monotone for subrank and degeneration is monotone for border subrank. The set $\{Q(T^{\otimes n})^{1/n}:n\ge1\}$ is nonempty and bounded by $R(T)$, and its supremum defines $\widetilde Q(T)$. All three invariants are zero on the zero tensor and equal $r$ on $\langle r\rangle$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Zero is an admissible target. Rank bounds every diagonal restriction target, and border rank bounds every diagonal degeneration target, giving finite attained maxima. Submultiplicativity of rank uniformly bounds the subrank roots. Normalization follows from the unit-power lower bound and the diagonal rank upper bound.

nodes.title: Finiteness forces unit normalization and the upper endpoint
nodes.notes: The real parameter is arbitrary; no admissible-interval hypothesis or circular appeal to normalization is used. Finiteness is established before converting values to real numbers.
nodes.statement_tex: If $V_\tau(\langle1\rangle)<\infty$, then $V_\tau(\langle1\rangle)=1$, $V_\tau(\langle r\rangle)=r$, $V_\tau(\langle\ell,m,n\rangle)=(\ell mn)^\tau$, and $V_\tau(T)\le\widetilde R(T)$ for every tensor. Consequently $\tau\le\omega/3$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Supermultiplicativity gives $V_\tau(\langle1\rangle)^2\le V_\tau(\langle1\rangle)$; the score-one witness gives the reverse lower bound by one. Under finiteness these imply unit normalization. Apply the scaling laws, rank restriction sources, positive-power multiplicativity, and the infimum of rank roots. At the size-two matrix tensor the bound becomes $8^\tau\le2^\omega$.

nodes.title: An explicit quadratic diagonal degeneration
nodes.notes: This elementary quadratic bound is sufficient for lower-parameter divergence and is distinct from the sharper cited bound. The degeneration works over every commutative semiring and includes q=0.
nodes.statement_tex: For every $q\ge0$, $\langle2q,2q,2q\rangle\trianglerighteq\langle q^2\rangle$. Over fields, $q^2\le\underline Q(\langle2q,2q,2q\rangle)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Index the target diagonal by pairs $(i,j)$ with $0\le i,j<q$, selecting source edges $(i,j)$, $(j,i+j)$, and $(i,i+j)$. Use the nonnegative natural weights $(i+j)^2$, $q^2+u^2-v^2$, and $4q^2-2w(w+z)$ on the three target factors. On the support, their sum is $5q^2$ plus a square, with equality exactly when all target pairs coincide. Apply the monomial degeneration criterion and reindex the $q^2$ pairs.

nodes.title: Prove2Me exponent identification and nine-quarters corollary
nodes.notes: External statement downloaded from Prove2Me on 2026-11-02; source URLs and hashes are preserved in material/prove2me/provenance.json. Its definition bodies are unchanged. The tensor bridge accounts for the reversed third-factor indices and includes zero dimensions. Equality of exponents is proved independently of the nine-quarters bound; the exact public target mme_omega_le_225 then follows from our main theorem. No external solution is imported.
nodes.statement_tex: For every field $K$, the downloaded Prove2Me exponent satisfies $\operatorname{MME.matMulExp}(K)=\omega_K\le 9/4=2.25$. Here $\operatorname{MME.matMulExp}$ is the infimum of $\log R(\mathrm{MM}_n)/\log n$ for $n\ge2$, with value $3$ at sizes zero and one, using pure-tensor decompositions in a tensor product of vector spaces.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Take coordinates in the tensor-product standard basis, reversing the third pair of indices. Pure-tensor decompositions and diagonal restrictions have the same lengths, so the two ordinary ranks agree. Asymptotic rank gives $\omega_K\le\log R(\mathrm{MM}_n)/\log n$ for $n\ge2$. Along $n=2^k$, these ratios converge to $\omega_K$, proving equality of the infima; $\omega_K\le3$ handles the two small sizes. Rewrite the downloaded target using this equality and apply the manuscript main theorem.

nodes.title: Rational restrictions and border rank
nodes.statement_tex: A restriction of scalar-extended tensors over $F(\varepsilon)$ gives a degeneration over $F$. Consequently $\underline R_F(T)\le R_{F(\varepsilon)}(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: The factor-map output is the constant rational tensor, hence regular at zero. Apply rational-to-polynomial degeneration equivalence to a minimal diagonal restriction witness.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Derivation supplied in the corresponding revised manuscript passage.

nodes.title: Asymptotic Gamma coefficient
nodes.notes: The manuscript supplies a Stirling derivation; the formal proof uses Euler’s limit formula.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Euler’s Gamma limit gives the Gamma quotient limit directly. Multiplication by the elementary prefactor yields the coefficient.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Derivation supplied in the corresponding revised manuscript passage.

nodes.title: Certified Gamma coefficient enclosure
nodes.notes: The decimal assertion is stated without a manuscript derivation. The library supplies exact rational certificates.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Bound $\Gamma(4/3)^{-3}$ between monotone rational product sequences and evaluate at $n=320$. Compare the cubes of the decimal endpoints using exact arithmetic.

nodes.title: Arithmetic-operation interpretation of the exponent
nodes.notes: The equality of the tensor-rank exponent with an arithmetic-operation exponent is conventional background, not formalized here. ExponentInfimum and the Prove2Me bridge compare tensor-rank definitions only; the project contains no computational model.
nodes.statement_tex: The introduction describes the exponent through asymptotic arithmetic-operation counts. The formal theorem uses the tensor-rank exponent defined in the preliminaries.

nodes.title: Factor-map definition of restriction
nodes.statement_tex: $T\ge S$ means that $(g_1\otimes g_2\otimes g_3)T=S$ for three linear factor maps.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Use the coefficient-array factor-map definition.

nodes.title: Polynomial-witness form of degeneration
nodes.statement_tex: Rational specialization is equivalent to polynomial factor maps satisfying $(g_1(\varepsilon)\otimes g_2(\varepsilon)\otimes g_3(\varepsilon))T=\varepsilon^dS+\varepsilon^{d+1}U(\varepsilon)$ for $d\ge0$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Clear rational denominators, factor their lowest power of the parameter, and normalize the remaining nonzero constant coefficient. This also treats a zero target. Conversely divide out the polynomial witness order.

nodes.title: Power multiplicativity of asymptotic rank
nodes.statement_tex: For $N\ge1$, $\widetilde R(T^{\otimes N})=\widetilde R(T)^N$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Compare the rank-root limit along multiples of the exponent.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Derivation supplied in the corresponding revised manuscript passage.

nodes.title: Asymptotic rank under degeneration
nodes.notes: The exact binomial coefficient bound is checked separately. The existing limit proof retains its coarser quadratic overhead, which is sufficient to prove the same conclusion over every field.
nodes.statement_tex: If $S\trianglelefteq T$, then $\widetilde R(S)\le\widetilde R(T)$. In particular, $\widetilde R(T)\le\underline R(T)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Extract degree $dN$ coefficients from the tensor-power polynomial witness. There are $\binom{dN+2}{2}$ restrictions. Bound their ranks, take $N$-th roots, and remove the polynomial overhead. Apply the result to a minimal border-rank witness.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Derivation supplied in the corresponding revised manuscript passage.

nodes.title: The leading-coefficient witness used in rank comparison
nodes.statement_tex: A degeneration admits polynomial maps with $(g_1\otimes g_2\otimes g_3)T=\varepsilon^dS+\varepsilon^{d+1}U(\varepsilon)$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Choose a polynomial degeneration witness.
nodes.manuscript_proof_note: Derivation supplied in the corresponding revised manuscript passage.

nodes.title: Matrix-size comparison by floor and ceiling powers
nodes.statement_tex: For $m\ge1$, $n\ge2$, $\ell=\lfloor m\log_2n\rfloor$, and $k=\lceil m\log_2n\rceil$, $\langle2,2,2\rangle^{\otimes\ell}\le\langle n,n,n\rangle^{\otimes m}\cong\langle n^m,n^m,n^m\rangle\le\langle2,2,2\rangle^{\otimes k}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Bound the integer matrix sizes using floor and ceiling logarithms; apply dimension restrictions and tensor-power equivalences.

nodes.title: The induced quotient bilinear map
nodes.notes: The manuscript states the quotient construction and its consequence without a separate proof. The formalization supplies well-definedness, the representative formula, uniqueness, and the degeneration.
nodes.statement_tex: Under the compatible-map hypotheses, $\bar\varphi:U\times(V/\operatorname{im}\iota_V)\to W/\operatorname{im}\iota_W$, $\bar\varphi(u,[v])=[\varphi(u,v)]$, exists uniquely. If $\iota_W$ is injective, $T_\varphi\trianglerighteq T_{\varphi_0}\diamondplus T_{\bar\varphi}$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Compatibility sends the input image into the output image, so quotient lifting constructs a bilinear map. Surjectivity of the quotient projection gives uniqueness. Apply the compatible-map degeneration theorem to the quotient projections.

nodes.statement_tex: For admissible $\tau$ and $a\ge1$, $P_\tau(a,a)\ge G(a)\ge a^{4/3}$.

nodes.title: Finite-product expression for the Gamma lower bound
nodes.statement_tex: $P_\tau(a,a)\ge\frac{3a-1}{2}\prod_{i=1}^{a-1}\frac{3i+1}{3i}=\frac{3a-1}{2}\prod_{i=1}^{a-1}\frac{i+1/3}{i}=\frac{3a-1}{2}\frac{\Gamma(a+1/3)}{\Gamma(4/3)\Gamma(a)}=G(a)$ for $a\ge1$. The parameter satisfies $2/3\le\tau\le\omega/3$.
nodes.proof_plan_tex: Iterate the Gamma functional equation and simplify the products termwise. Apply the checked exact lower bound.
